cbps_claim_ladder.forbidden_claim: The no-range poker AR model has ordered opponent-belief tracking.
cbps_claim_ladder.paper_safe_claim: Positive hidden-state range probes are insufficient evidence for ordered belief tracking. For the no-range poker AR row, the best-supported diagnostic interpretation is composition-bounded predictive support: behavior prediction is positive, while strict matched-composition gates block an ordered-belief claim.

rows.allowed_claim: The audit can distinguish posterior, composition, and CBPS known states in a synthetic control.
The no-range poker AR row is behavior-predictive but composition-bounded under the locked audit.

order_intervention.allowed_paper_claim: Under input-level same-composition order permutations, the frozen poker AR can be audited for order sensitivity. This is a stress test, not a legal poker causal proof.
order_intervention.forbidden_paper_claim: This input permutation proves or disproves ordered opponent-belief tracking.

probe_capacity_s6_s7.claim_rule: MLP rows are appendix-only and can only create a capacity caveat, not replace main linear rows.

range_rank_sensitivity.allowed_paper_claim: Range-probe behavior-footprint conclusions can be reported as stable or rank-sensitive across the predeclared rank grid. This is a sensitivity stress test, not causal mediation.
range_rank_sensitivity.forbidden_paper_claim: Rank sensitivity proves the presence or absence of belief tracking or a causal circuit.

range_subspace.allowed_paper_claim: Top range-probe subspace ablation can be compared with same-rank random subspace ablation as a behavior-footprint stress test. It is not a causal mediation proof.
range_subspace.forbidden_paper_claim: This subspace ablation proves the range-correlated hidden directions causally drive policy.
